title: Compare seasonal forecasts across three origins
summary: Run a seasonal-naive forecast and one four-week averaging change on identical 28-day windows. This small original teaching lab demonstrates the workflow; it does not reproduce an M5 entry.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.14 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64. This local CPU run is the recorded environment; other environments are not covered by this receipt.
steps: Download the script. Use Python 3.12.14; no packages, account or data download are needed for the fixture.
Run the command and compare the per-series results at each of the three origins. Freeze those windows before interpreting the aggregate.
Explain why the methods differ and which series/origin changes your conclusion. Keep an underperforming change in the receipt.

To use authorized daily data, replace --fixture with --csv your-data.csv. Required columns: series,day,sales; each series has unique contiguous days starting at 1 and at least 168 rows. This optional mode was tested on a generated CSV fixture, not M5 data.
limitations: The generated two-series fixture is not M5 competition data.
Unweighted MAE excludes M5 WRMSSE weights, hierarchy and scaling. It cannot be compared to a competition score.
This run establishes neither historical solution reproduction nor reader learning.
Elapsed time and traced Python memory cover this local script run, not a final competition pipeline.
split_definition: Three fixed rolling origins: days 1–84, 1–112 and 1–140 train; next 28 days validate for each series.
metric: mean absolute error (unweighted; not M5 WRMSSE)

project.outcome: Run a seasonal-naive forecast and one four-week averaging change on identical 28-day windows. This small original teaching lab demonstrates the workflow; it does not reproduce an M5 entry.
prerequisites: Run a Python script locally and read per-split metric results.

access.instructions: Use the generated teaching fixture with --fixture. Optional private inputs require your own authorized access; they have not been verified by this receipt.
access.authorization: Original generated teaching fixture distributed with the script; no competition files required.

project.baseline: Fit seasonal-naive using training rows only on the fixed declared splits.
project.controlled_change: Compare four-week-mean on exactly the same splits; a worse metric is a valid outcome.
diagnostics: Inspect every recorded split and compare the direction and size of the method difference.
Explain the split assumption and at least one limit before choosing another experiment.

troubleshooting.recovery: Use the pinned Python version, inspect the script error, and rerun the fixture before attempting authorized private inputs.
